card.name: Fakaseasea
card.tagline: The slow praise-song dance of Tuvalu.
card.profile: Fakaseasea is a slow traditional Tuvaluan dance-song, historically performed mainly by young women standing and moving arms, hands and upper body while singers beat time on a slit drum or tea chest. Distinguished by very loose rules and island-specific variations, it was composed in praise of an aliki or toa and to honor canoe-building, house construction and fishing. Unlike the fakanau and oga, which died out, the fakaseasea survived, though now performed chiefly by elders for celebratory and remembrance occasions.
card.insight: The Tuvaluan funeral tradition kupu is described as similar to fakaseasea, linking the form to mourning practice. (Wikipedia, Music of Tuvalu)
